recipes.name: Moist Holiday Honeycake
ingredients_raw: 1 cup strong brewed coffee (decaf is fine)

steps.text: Place an oven rack in an upper position in the oven. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Spray a 10-inch fluted tube pan (such as Bundt) with cooking spray.

In a bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, cloves, and nutmeg until thoroughly combined. In a separate large bowl, whisk together canola oil, honey, white and brown sugars, eggs, vanilla, coffee, orange juice, and whiskey. With an electric mixer, beat the flour mixture into the honey mixture just until thoroughly incorporated. Pour the batter into the prepared pan.

Bake on the upper shelf of the preheated oven until golden brown and a toothpick inserted into the center comes out with moist crumbs, about 1 hour. Cool for 20 minutes in the pan before turning out onto a serving platter.

raw_recipe.headline: Moist Holiday Honeycake
raw_recipe.description: Serve this moist honey cake for the Jewesh New Year of Rosh Hashanah and delight all of your guests with its fragrant aroma and yummy taste.

review.reviewBody: I thought this recipe looked familiar. This is Marcy Goldman's "Majestic and Moist New Yesr's Honey Cake" recipe out of her cookbook, A Treasury of Jewish Holiday Baking. The only variation is nutmeg instead of allspice, canola oil instead of vegetable oil, and the sliced or slivered almonds on top. None the less the very best Honey cake ever. I've been making it for years for holiday's and all year round and would never think of using a different recipe. Two notes, almonds are sprinkled on top prior to baking and you should let it cool in the pan for about 15 - 20 min and then invert onto a wire rack to cool completely before placing it on a serving platter.
I made this for a Feast of Trumpets celebration and it turned out good. I had no trouble getting it out of the pan like some because I greased and floured the pan and waited until completely cool.

I've been using it for years. I've made in a tube pan, bundt pan and 3 8"x4" loaf pans, which is my favorite method because then some can be frozen for later. I've made it many times as written, and also have reduced the white sugar to 1 cup to make it a little less sweet and both are good. It stays moist for days so I usually make it several days before Rosh Hashanah.

I made this reciep for my Synagogue. since I was feeding so many and they asked for small portions, I used a silicone mold in the shape of small blossoms. I cooked them for 25 minutes at 350 and they came out beautiful. I also used honey whiskey instead of regular. it was a hit.

Dee-Lish!! Everyone loved this cake. Very moist and fragrant. Easy to make. I made the following small adjustments: 3/4 cup honey, 1/2 cup molasses; omitted whiskey; reduced sugar to 3/4 C white sugar; 1/2 C brown sugar.
In my oven it was done in 50 minutes.
Thank you for this recipe!

I made this cake for my children. I skipped the whiskey and orange juice but otherwise followed the recipe. I glazed the cake with a mixture of honey, brown sugar, butter, and vanilla essence. Next time I will poke holes in the cake first to let the glaze soak in for maximum moisture.

Made this as muffins, and had some left over for a shallow loaf. It is very moist and honey-sweet without an overpowering taste of honey. I may have gone a bit easy on the coffee since I don't like it as a rule, but surprisingly none of the individual flavors come through noticeably. If you want it to taste of the whisky or spice you'll need to up the amounts. Apart from scaling down the quantity, I'd make it again.
Great cake, both in taste and texture (it's like a spice cake). I find, however, that only 1/4 C each of white and brown sugar is sufficient.
So MOIST! Followed the recipes exactly. I used a standard Bundt pan and the battered overflowed dramatically. Next time I will use a Bundt pan AND a small loaf pan.

I have to say, I made this for Rosh Hashana dinner despite my lifelong dislike of honey cake. True to its name, it was moist and full of flavor. I used bourbon for the whiskey, and while not overpowering, it really gave a distinct and warm flavor to the cake. People were skeptical since honey cake is always such a disappointment, but this one really was wonderful. Thank you Amybobamy!

This is a lovely cake. I didn't have any orange juice at home so had to use pineapple instead and still taste great! As I'm in Australia i also substituted the all purpose flour baking powder/soda and salt for Self raising flour. I iced mine with a lemon glaze. Really nice different flavour. Thank you
I made this exactly as per the recipe and by far it is the most flavourful moist honey cake, and everybody raved about it this Rosh Hashanah.
Easy to make and tasted gorgeous, definitely on our weekly menu now!
Family loved it Moist, great flavors Perfect for Bundt pan!
Great every time I make it!
Absolutely amazing!! I was out of OJ & ground nutmeg, so subbed pineapple juice & allspice. I’ll definitely be making this again, but will be sure to have all the ingredients on hand.

My gma was from Austria , (came to N.Y. in 1905) and made Honey Cake all the time. This recipe is easy and great! It is very moist a little stickey how it should be!I've tried to find some recipes and this is by far the best!
I made this cake as written as was pleased with the results. Fantastic use of spices.

I uused the star of David pan that is pictured, but it is too small for the batter. It ran over! 
Other than the mess at the bottom of my oven, this cake is delicious!!

We loved this cake! I only wished I had noted the size of the bundt pan listed as mine cooked over and made a mess. Live and learn. I have requests to make it again, so will use the extra batter for cupcakes.
